title: Sprite/Asset Generator?
author: itsDitch
selftext:
Hi all

I've been having some success working with opus / antigravity and phaser to build our 2D games

The biggest hurdle for me at the moment seems to be asset generation, ai tools are very good now at sticking to a reference image, but creating a Sprite sheet for animations seems to be a challenge

Any recommendations for solid tools with free trials I can test out and see if they are good enough?

comments.author: blackwidowink
comments.body: I recommend Autosprite.io. They have a free trial and daily credits you can use to check it out. I’ve used their animations for a couple of games now.

replies.author: FutureLynx_
replies.body: looks nice though their daily credits are a bit too low.

replies.author: blackwidowink
replies.body: I ended up buying the lowest monthly subscription…which is $8 I think. I don’t usually run out of credits and they roll over I believe.

comments.author: estebansaa
comments.body: You can use Nano Banana on Replicate, simply give it a layout, a template as reference of the assets you need.

comments.author: thelionskywalker
comments.body: I think dreamforge.ai has really really good asset studio. You have to send a game prompt to access it though but you can just write create nothing to save credits. 1500 credits in the free plan which takes you a long way.

comments.author: Tsjo_Wi
comments.body: You can sign up for unity ai beta for free. I've made some pretty cool things with the spritesheet generator (model seedance 1 pro). You can upload a start frame (and optional end frame) and prompt what it should animate, and it will spit out a 16 frame spritesheet.

comments.author: Straight-Tea-8564
comments.body:
I’ll try to explain this in a straightforward way, because I went through the same thing at the beginning and I can share what actually worked for me.

Generating spritesheets or frame-by-frame animations with traditional image AIs is still in its early stages. It’s not fully reliable. When you try to place multiple characters in the same image, the AI tends to hallucinate details and the frames often come out inconsistent.

What I’ve been doing, and what I see many other people doing, is generating animations using video AI instead.

It’s not the cheapest process yet, but the results are worth it.

On replicate.com you’ll find several video AI models. Veo3 is one of the best options right now, but it’s still quite expensive. I recommend taking a look at Seedance Pro, especially because it supports first and last frame input.

The idea is simple. You upload two frames. If you want to create a walk cycle, for example, you upload the character already prepared to start walking, you can even use two identical frames, and then ask the AI to generate the video from that.

The key detail is this. Before uploading your image, create a chroma key background. It can be green or pink, but always choose a color opposite to your character. For example, if you’re making a goblin, which is usually green, use a pink background. That way, once the video is generated, it becomes much easier to remove the background.

There are tools for this. I actually built one myself using Vibecode to convert the video into a PNG sequence and automatically remove the background.

Here’s a project I’m currently developing entirely with characters created through this process:

https://polargames.com.br/files/rpg-tatics/rpg-tatics.mp4

replies.author: itsDitch
replies.body: Nice! I had the idea of using video earlier but just hadn't figured out the chroma key part. I have access to Google flow as part of my pro sub so can use that!

replies.author: itsDitch
replies.body: Hey, could you touch on the chroma key backgrounds a bit more please? do you create the image WITH the background, or provide it as an ingredient to the video? i'd also love to know more about your tool you built to convert

replies.author: Straight-Tea-8564
replies.body:
Yes, I already send the first and last frame with the chroma key color. The video returns the animation.

I created the tool with Vibecode. It detects the background and converts it into a PNG alpha channel. Then I export the frames or the spritesheet.  


https://preview.redd.it/v3wzr5vu4jhg1.png?width=1024&format=png&auto=webp&s=22f5cc97db9592ce65379d9a1b1ec1d2a9df1a13

replies.author: Dramatic-Wish-5696
replies.body: This doesn't work very well; AI video has a lot of blur, some frames are blurry, and there's no way to extract the background correctly.

replies.author: Straight-Tea-8564
replies.body: It works well, but requires a lot of refinement. I use another AI to convert to 4K and 60 fps, and now the background removal is perfect.

comments.author: mike402
comments.body: The best sprite animator is at Ludo.ai and they just rolled out an MCP, so you can just have your agent generate all your sprite sheets :)

comments.author: beelllllll
comments.body:
This is why I ended up building [https://www.autosprite.io/](https://www.autosprite.io/) 

I'm biased but I find it's the best out there for making animated spritesheets of characters, but there is always room for improvement. Try it out and if you have any feedback I would be happy to hear.
